story.name: ジョニーの たび
story.title: Snowed In in Vermont
story.line: ジョニーが ゆきの やまごやの はなしを します
story.ja: コンパスなしで乗った船は、まちがえてボストン行きだった。ジョニーはバスで北へ向かい、バーモントの山小屋に住む昔の船乗り仲間ルースを訪ねる。大雪で停電し、3日間とじこめられる。まきストーブ、トランプ、雪にメープルシロップをかけるお菓子。帰りぎわ、ルースは日本の古い絵はがきをくれた。

segments.en: The next night was cooler, and the fire was a little bigger. Maple had brought a thermos of hot cider, and Kicks had brought his own folding chair.
Okay, okay, so you lost the compass. Then what? Did you get on the wrong ship or something?
How did you know? That's exactly what happened. I got on a big cargo ship, and a month later, I was in Boston.
Boston in March is not a place for a sailor in a thin jacket. The wind came off the harbor like it had something personal against him.
So Gulliver did what any sensible bird would do. He bought a wool hat, a very large coffee, and a bus ticket north.
I have an old shipmate in Vermont. Ruth. We sailed together for years, and then she retired to a cabin in the woods.
The bus wound its way up into the hills. Little white churches, red barns, and snow on everything, like someone had covered the world in frosting.
Ruth met him at the bus stop in an old pickup truck. She was wearing a red plaid coat and the same big grin he remembered.
First thing she said was, you look terrible. Second thing she said was, get in, there's soup.
The cabin was small and made of logs, with a wood stove in the middle that kept the whole place warm and smelling like pine.
That night, it started to snow. Not the light, pretty kind. The serious kind, the kind that doesn't plan on stopping.
By morning, the snow was halfway up the windows, and the power was out. They were snowed in, and the whole world was quiet and white.
Oh my gosh, that sounds so cozy. Weren't you scared, though, being stuck out there?
Not one bit. Ruth said, out here, you don't fight the snow. You just make more soup and wait it out.
So that's what they did. They kept the stove going, played cards by candlelight, and told the same old sea stories they had told a hundred times.
Ruth cheated at cards. Gulliver knew it, and Ruth knew he knew it, and neither of them said a word about it.
On the second day, Ruth said she had a treat for him. She heated a pot of maple syrup on the stove until it was bubbling.
Then she went outside, packed a pan full of clean, fresh snow, and poured the hot syrup over it in thin lines.
It turns into this soft, chewy candy, right there on the snow. You pick it up with a fork. They call it sugar on snow.
Wait, wait. Maple syrup on snow? Okay, I need to try that. Like, right now.
And here's the strange part. She served it with a plain donut and a sour pickle on the side.
A pickle? Come on, man. You're making that up. Nobody eats a pickle with candy.
I swear on my cap. The pickle cuts the sweetness, so you can keep eating. It's a Vermont thing. And it works.
On the third day, they heard a low rumble through the trees.
It was the snowplow, pushing a clean path down the road. And the power came back on.
Gulliver was almost sad. He had gotten used to the quiet, and to losing at cards.
Before he left, Ruth took a faded postcard out of an old wooden box.
It showed a small white ferry on a calm blue sea, with green islands all around.
She said, it's in Japan. The Seto Inland Sea. I always meant to go and never did. So you go, and tell me about it.
Gulliver put the postcard in his inside pocket, right where the compass used to be. And that's where he kept it, the whole way across the world.
Dude, that's actually really sweet. Did you ever write to her?
Not yet. I'm still working on it. But first, I have to tell you about the ferry. Tomorrow night.
Maple poured the last of the cider. And somewhere far away, it was snowing on a little log cabin in the woods.

predict.ask: ジョニーは 日本の フェリーで どうなる？
choices: He gets seasick and stays in his cabin the whole time.
He falls asleep on the ferry and keeps missing his stop.
He finds Ruth waiting for him on one of the islands.
predict.ja: フェリーで寝てしまい、何度も降りそびれる。
